item.title: Braves Must Sign Freddy Peralta To Sting The Mets
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Mets made a huge mistake letting Freddy Peralta walk away, and now they face a painful reality. According to Yahoo Sports , a long-term contract for Peralta by the Braves would hurt the Mets if he competes against them for years in the NL East. Last year the Mets did not maximize his performance, so they may now witness his dominance in a different uniform. Following his trade, Peralta ended the regular season with a 3.25 ERA over 10 starts for the Tampa Bay Rays. His final six regular season starts showed a 0.79 ERA for the Rays, demonstrating increased sharpness late in the year. Atlanta would stabilize a shaky rotation lacking a clear number two starter by acquiring him. While the Braves have choices, no option guarantees the solution they require immediately. Although Chris Sale is a veteran, the team considers younger arms such as AJ Smith-Shawver and Spencer Schwellenbach as possible rotation options. Grant Holmes and Bryce Elder are also on the roster, while Spencer Strider remains a major uncertainty following his injuries. Although signing Peralta cannot fix all Braves rotation problems, it constitutes a positive first move. The Mets Will Pay the Price Acquiring Peralta strikes the Mets in their pride and their standings, causing the most pain. The Mets obtained him last offseason but observed his struggles before sending him to Tampa Bay. Now he has regained form, and if he dons a Braves jersey, each outing against New York will feel like betrayal. By signing Peralta to a long-term deal, the Braves could inflict pain on the Mets through years of divisional games. Fixing the rotation is vital for Atlanta, and compensating Peralta would make an excellent start. His ability to defeat any lineup is evident, and the Mets understand precisely what they forfeited. A Hot Arm for the NL East A Braves signing would secure a pitcher currently hot and a player skilled at beating the team in the neighboring city. The Mets likely regret failing to unlock Peralta’s potential last year.

item.title: Eagles player admits contract worries hurt his play — now Cowboys game could change his future
item.description: PHILADELPHIA — Eagles edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie is only making $4.3 million as the team’s fourth pass rusher this season. Ebiketie is playing on a cheap one-year deal, but the Eagles have provided a good situation for him even though he’s not making a ton of money. He played 91.1% of the defensive snaps (72) in the team’s Week 6 loss to the Carolina Panthers. Now, he could make his first start of the season against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday night after starting edge rushers Jonathan Greenard and Jalyx Hunt were listed as questionable. Edge rusher Nolan Smith was also ruled out after suffering a concussion last week. Ebiketie signed with the Eagles this past offseason after spending four seasons with the Atlanta Falcons. Before getting demoted to a rotational role in 2025, he recorded 14.5 sacks over three seasons as a starter. The Eagles gave Ebiketie a fresh start. He feels rejuvenated. “I’m more at ease,” Ebiketie told NJ.com on Saturday. “I’m not stressed at all.” Ebiketie knows what’s at stake this season. When he becomes a free agent in March, the 27-year-old pass rusher could draw more interest from other NFL teams and earn a bigger contract if he plays well for the Eagles. “Obviously, that’s the case,” Ebiketie said about wanting to improve his value as an impending free agent. “But mentally in the past, given the fact that last year I was in the final year of my contract in Atlanta, I felt like that came into play a little bit and sometimes was a distraction. “I feel like this year for me, it’s just one snap at a time. Every time I go out there, I am trying to put my best foot forward. At the end of the day, at the end of the year, you’re going to look back and see what you put on film. That’s who you are.” Ebiketie recorded a career-low 18 tackles and two sacks during his final season with the Falcons. He might have cost himself money. “It was a little bit of both,” Ebiketie said about feeling frustrated and worried last season. “When the organization drafted two guys [in the first round], it’s probably an indication that they are moving in a different direction. Having to worry about everything and not really having the same opportunity that I had in the years past got me to think further out [about my future]. From that standpoint, I grew from that because I could have just focused on what I was doing, and I think that led me to miss a couple opportunities. I worried about things that I shouldn’t be worried about.” Nearly a year removed from that situation, Ebiketie no longer fixates on his snap count. item.title: Why is Wilcox in line of fire from Man Utd fans?
item.description: Jason Wilcox (fourth from left) watched United's 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth alongside chief executive Omar Berrada [Getty Images] As the clocked ticked down during Manchester United's 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday, the home fans made it clear what they thought about director of football Jason Wilcox. Singing his name along with an obscenity, the message was brutal and to the point. It was sung by a majority of the United supporters, and on more than one occasion. It came less than two weeks after United defender Lisandro Martinez had launched a blistering attack on the club's hierarchy for not strengthening the squad, with a particular message for Wilcox. "I expect more from our technical director," said Martinez. Pressure is growing on United boss Michael Carrick after eight games without a win - their worst run since 2015-16 - and two three-goal defeats in a week. But focus is turning to Wilcox too. End approaching for Carrick but Man Utd fans make clear who they blame Why is Wilcox under pressure? Wilcox is a former England winger who won the Premier League with Blackburn in 1994-95. He joined United in April 2024 - initially as technical director after 15 months in a similar role at Manchester City, where he had previously been in charge of the academy. At City he worked with current United chief executive Omar Berrada and also Stephen Torpey, who was appointed United's head of academy in August 2025. When he arrived, it was said by United officials that Wilcox would work across all technical areas of the club to achieve "highest standards of performance" and would be answerable to the sporting director. That changed the following December, when that sporting director - Dan Ashworth - was sacked amid a difference of opinion over who should replace Erik ten Hag as manager. Ten months on, a poor series of results and dissatisfaction with transfer business has put Wilcox in the spotlight. There are some who have sympathy with the position Wilcox finds himself in. The 55-year-old is not in charge of transfer budgets, which are set at a higher level. Wilcox was also - obviously - not responsible for the injury Manuel Ugarte sustained playing for Uruguay at the World Cup, which wrecked a plan to sell the midfielder in the summer to bolster the transfer budget. He, too, was powerless to prevent Barcelona backing out of a £26m deal to sign England forward Marcus Rashford. Both issues affected the amount United could spend in the summer - both on transfer fees and wages. item.title: Chiefs’ offense had a historically poor showing in loss to Seahawks
item.description: (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images This season, the Kansas City Chiefs reinvigorated the offense around quarterback Patrick Mahomes and started generating explosive plays again, whether through handoffs to running back Kenneth Walker or downfield throws off play action. In Week 7, the Seattle Seahawks kept the Chiefs from finding any long gains, and suddenly, the offense looked as horrendous as it has in any game in the era of quarterback Patrick Mahomes. The Chiefs did not reach the red zone or the end zone against Seattle. Since 2016, that's happened to teams 56 times. It had never happened to a Patrick Mahomes-led team before tonight. — SūmerSports (@SumerSports) October 26, 2026 Mahomes finished with 165 yards on 19 of 33 passing, posting the fifth-lowest marks of his career for passing yards per attempt (5) and passer rating (58.3). It was only the second time Kansas City has scored three or fewer points with Mahomes at quarterback. The other game was also in Week 7, in 2021, a 27-3 loss to the Tennessee Titans . According to NFL Researcher on X , the Chiefs totaled the fewest yards and first downs of any game started by Mahomes. It was a frustrating night for the two-time MVP, who played without two of his top wideouts — Rashee Rice (hamstring) and Tyquan Thornton (dislocated ankle) — and his starting right tackle, Jaylon Moore (concussion). Still, Mahomes and the Chiefs’ offense have produced more in similarly tough spots before. It was a failure from start to finish in Seattle. Head coach Andy Reid pointed to one key factor in the abysmal performance after the game in his post-game press conference. “You got to keep yourself out of third-and-long situations,” Reid said at the podium. “You’ve got to do better on first and second down. We can do better. We had some penalties in there also that got us going in the wrong direction. Got to take care of those.” On Kansas City’s opening drive, the Chiefs moved the chains on third-and-7, but the officials called an illegal shift on tight end Travis Kelce, wiping away any offensive momentum. Late in the first half, two incompletions opened a drive, and the Chiefs failed to convert on third-and-10 with a screen pass to running back Emmett Johnson. Those possessions put the Chiefs in a hole, and Mahomes couldn’t dig him and the unit out of it. He threw an interception on a second-down pass in Seattle territory that could’ve been avoided. He also fumbled on a third-down play when he didn’t feel the pressure, ending a promising possession. Mahomes reflected on the game at the podium in Seattle. “In order to have success in this league, you got to be able to sustain drives, and we weren’t able to do that,” Mahomes acknowledged. “And obviously they contained the explosive plays. So it’s stuff we have to continue to get better at. You can’t have those mistakes versus this defense.” At one point in the first half, Mahomes was 7/14 with an interception and just 63 yards. item.title: Barcelona suffer fresh defensive setback as Xavi Espart ruled out for seven weeks
item.description: Barcelona suffer fresh defensive setback as Xavi Espart ruled out for seven weeks Barcelona have suffered another injury setback after teenage defender Xavi Espart was ruled out for approximately seven weeks following Sunday’s 2-1 defeat to Real Madrid. The 19-year-old sustained an injury to his right ankle during El Clasico at the Camp Nou, forcing him off before the half-hour mark. Espart went to ground after experiencing discomfort and was unable to continue, with Alejandro Balde replacing him in the 29th minute. Barcelona subsequently confirmed the extent of the problem in a statement on Monday, estimating that the youngster would require around seven weeks to recover. The diagnosis represents a significant blow for Barcelona manager Hansi Flick, who is already dealing with several injuries across his squad. Espart is expected to miss nine first-team fixtures, including the important La Liga encounter against Atletico Madrid on November 8. The defender is also set to be unavailable for Barcelona’s Champions League meetings with Aston Villa and Manchester City. His absence comes at a particularly difficult time after the Catalan club suffered consecutive defeats in major competitions. Barcelona lost 4-2 to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League last week before Sunday’s defeat against their fiercest domestic rivals. The Clasico result reduced Barcelona’s advantage over second-placed Atletico to two points, with Real Madrid another point behind. Espart’s injury further complicates Flick’s defensive selection decisions, particularly with Andreas Christensen, Jules Kounde and Eric Garcia also sidelined. The German coach has increasingly relied on the versatile teenager during his breakthrough campaign. A product of Barcelona’s renowned La Masia academy, Espart has already started nine matches across La Liga and the Champions League this season. Although naturally a midfielder, he has primarily operated at left-back and can also provide cover on the opposite flank. His technical ability, positional flexibility and willingness to advance into attacking areas have made him a valuable option in Flick’s system. Espart delivered one of his most impressive performances against PSG, scoring his first Champions League goal despite Barcelona’s defeat. The youngster has consequently emerged as one of the club’s most promising academy graduates, earning increased responsibility in a demanding campaign. With Joao Cancelo another option on the left, Flick must now consider how best to redistribute minutes while avoiding further disruption. Barcelona are also without attacking players Dani Olmo and Roony Bardghji, adding to the manager’s selection concerns. Espart’s projected recovery period could keep him out until mid-December, depending on his rehabilitation progress. For Barcelona, the immediate priority is navigating a challenging fixture schedule without another defender who has become increasingly important to their plans.

item.title: David Goffin issues emotional message after retiring from tennis career, ‘It is difficult to find the right words’
item.description: David Goffin’s professional tennis career has concluded. Goffin, a former finalist at the ATP Finals, bid farewell to his storied career on the professional circuit after losing to Alex Michelsen in the Brussels Open second round. The six-time ATP champion issued a heartfelt speech in the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s contest, reflecting on the sacrifices his family have made throughout his career, while also thanking his coaching team. Goffin has now issued another – equally heartfelt – statement on social media. David Goffin’s parting message as he closes ATP chapter “It is difficult to find the right words to describe all the emotions that are in my head today,” Goffin said in a social media post published on Monday morning. “First there is nostalgia, the one that takes me back to my first moments on a tennis court, to that first racket held in my hands, to that very last ball struck in Brussels. “A moment that I was anticipating, necessarily full of emotion, but you managed to turn it into a memory as beautiful and unforgettable. I will forever keep this ovation, this fervor and all the love you showed me at the end of my last game. “From the bottom of my heart, thank you for accompanying me, supporting and encouraging me all these years, in all corners of the world. “Your applause, encouragement, shouts and words have been an invaluable source of strength and motivation. item.title: Michael Kim Says Tour Won’t Care If Players Get Pissed Off
item.description: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images The DP World Tour wants big names back, even if it means pushing aside the guys who stuck around when things got messy. Michael Kim laid out this hard reality during an X Q&A session on Sunday. He believes the tour leadership will happily accept Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton returning, regardless of the anger it causes lower-ranked players. Kim wrote that while the move might “prob pisses off some of the membership,” the tour “prob doesn’t care much about pissing off the 100th player on the tour.” They want the stars, not the sympathy. The Commercial Logic Wins Rahm and Hatton are not just returning players; they are the draw. Rahm holds 10 DP World Tour wins and two major titles, while Hatton has eight tour wins to his name. Their return is already set in motion with Rahm scheduled to play the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship from November 5-8. Hatton confirmed his plans on October 23, stating he would not join the new LIV 2.0 group. The tour needs this kind of buzz to keep sponsors happy and fans watching. But this isn’t just about the big two. The bigger issue involves a flood of other former LIV players seeking invitations. Eddie Pepperell argued that only a few specific names like Bryson DeChambeau or Cam Smith actually bring enough value to justify special access. He told Yahoo Sports that inviting others is a mistake. Pepperell wrote, “None of these players are going to put enough bums on seats or in front of TVs to materially improve the balance sheet in 2027, period.” If the tour ignores this and hands out too many invites, they risk diluting the value of the very spots they are fighting to fill. The Cost to Loyal Players While the tour chases headlines, the players who stayed loyal are watching their opportunities shrink. Dutch pro Joost Luiten voiced the fear that many tournament invites will go to LIV returnees instead of rising local talent. “My concern is that many of the tournament invitations will end up going to LIV players, leaving fewer opportunities for young talents and local players,” Luiten told GolfMagic. He emphasized that the issue is about protecting the future of the tour and respecting those who never left. Sean Crocker just fought for his own spot at the Genesis Championship, rallying from three-over par to finish 100th in the rankings and secure his card for 2027. He admitted, “A lot was going through my mind on that golf course today. I needed to play good, I was obviously hoping to get off to a way better start than I did.” Crocker’s struggle highlights the reality for everyone below the top tier. They have to grind every week to stay in the field, while the tour might hand out wild cards to names who haven’t played in Europe since 2001. Michael Kim summed it up best. item.description: What is the Ballon d'Or? Award history and why it matters so much to soccer players originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Every October, the Ballon d'Or is a huge bone of contention for soccer fans around the globe, as the prestigious award prepares to add another superstar to its list of all-time great winners. As the new club season begins, fans and media take one last look at the previous campaign to identify the best player around the world. Last year's men's winner Ousmane Dembele led Paris Saint-Germain to a second consecutive Champions League title, but he has challengers for the 2026 award thanks to those who excelled at the FIFA World Cup. The Sporting News looks at why the Ballon d'Or is so special and how the winner is selected. LIVE: Ballon d'Or 2026 updates as winners and final awards results are announced What is the Ballon d'Or? The Ballon d'Or, or "Golden Ball" in French, is the most prestigious individual award in world soccer, recognizing the best male and female players around the globe from the previous season. Some of the greatest the game has ever seen, such as Lionel Messi , Cristiano Ronaldo , Diego Maradona, Zinedine Zidane, and many others have been bestowed with the famous trophy. First launched and awarded in 1956 by French publication France Football, the Ballon d'Or has been given out in every single year since, only missing the 2020 season due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The 2027 event will be the 70th edition of the men's award. In 2018, the Ballon d'Or Feminin was introduced for the first time to honor the best female player in the world. How is the Ballon d'or decided? A panel of international journalists compiled by France Football comes up with the 30 finalists for the men's Ballon d'Or and the Yashin Award shortlist for the world's best goalkeeper. The voting process for the final award was revised in 2022 to involve a media member from each of the top 100 nations in the FIFA men's world ranking (for the men's Ballon d'Or voting) and from the top 50 nations in the FIFA women's world ranking (for the women's Ballon d'Or vote). The media members vote by selecting names from the list of finalists, and they rank their selections. Each vote is weighted with different point totals assigned based on the specific ranking of the player on the ballot. After all the votes are tallied, the player with the most points is awarded the Ballon d'Or. While the award was initially limited to recognizing the best European player on the continent, in 1995 organizers opened it up to non-Europeans plying their trade in Europe to also be considered. In 2007, the award was expanded further so any player across the world could be eligible whether or not they played in Europe. item.title: Amerks Hall of Fame adds John Tortorella, Nathan Paetsch
item.description: The Rochester Americans' storied history will be celebrated with two new inductees to the team's hall of fame in the coming months. Former defenseman Nathan Paetsch and coach John Tortorella are the latest to receive the organization's highest honor. The pair are the 2027 selections for the Amerks Hall of Fame, the 72nd and 73rd members. The induction ceremony is set for Saturday, Dec. 5, before the Amerks host the Belleville Senators. Paetsch spent parts of seven seasons as a player in Rochester, the second-most for any defenseman in team history. According to the team's press release , he's also one of only three players to start and finish their playing careers in Rochester. The 43-year-old finished his career with nearly 900 professional games and two Calder Cup wins. Paetsch retired prior to the 2021-22 season and took turns as a development coach for the Buffalo Sabres and assistant coach with the Amerks. "It's hard to say what this honor means to me. This organization helped raise me as a 20-year-old man and then helped me achieve my dream of playing in the NHL. I met my wife here and it instantly became my home. The Amerks aren't just a team I played and worked for, it's my family," Paetsch said in a statement. One of the most colorful personalities in the hockey world, Tortorella had a two-year stint as the Amerks' head coach. Previously an assistant with the parent Sabres, Tortorella was named the AHL team's bench boss prior to the 1995-96 season. He posted a record of 77 wins, 69 losses and 14 ties in those seasons, and guided Rochester to the Calder Cup championship in 1996. Tortorella is the eighth former head coach picked for the team's hall of fame. Following his time in Rochester, Tortorella spent the better part of 26 years coaching several teams in the NHL. He pushed the Tampa Bay Lightning to the Stanley Cup in 2004, and most recently led the Vegas Golden Knights to the Final. The Boston native ranks ninth in NHL history with 777 career wins, second-most among American-born coaches. Tortorella is a two-time winner of the NHL's Jack Adams Award as the league's top coach. "The time I spent in Rochester was such an important part of my career and I'm grateful to have had the opportunity, even if it was just for those two seasons," Tortorella said. "I am truly appreciative of this tremendous honor and look forward to being back in Rochester for the first time in a long time." The Amerks (4-3-1) have two more games to wrap October: Wednesday vs. the Hershey Bears and Friday against the Lehigh Valley Phantoms. item.title: Can anyone save Anthony Richardson’s before he is out of chances?
item.description: Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. (5) warms up Thursday, Aug. 14, 2025, at a joint practice with the Green Bay Packers during training camp at Grand Park in Westfield. Anthony Richardson was supposed to be the next quarterback who broke the NFL. At 6-foot-4 with a cannon for an arm and rare running ability, the 2023 fourth overall pick looked like a cheat code waiting to happen. Instead, he has become a warning about confusing potential with progress. Through three seasons, Richardson has completed just 50.6% of his passes, with 11 touchdowns and 13 interceptions across 17 appearances. Injuries have limited his chances, including a season-ending orbital fracture in 2025. But the numbers point to a bigger problem than bad luck: the Indianapolis Colts still haven’t seen enough consistent quarterback play to trust him as their starter. The tools were never the problem Richardson entered the league with only 13 starts at Florida. That made him an extraordinary athlete and an unusually unfinished quarterback prospect. The Colts drafted the ceiling, betting coaching and game reps could close the gap between his physical gifts and his fundamentals. That bet has not paid off. His completion rate fell from 59.5% in four games as a rookie to 47.7% in 2024. He can make spectacular throws and punish defenses as a runner, but routine accuracy, timing, and consistency have been harder to find. The infamous decision to tap out of a game in 2024 also raised questions about his readiness for the demands of being an NFL starter, though one moment should not define his entire career. Injuries matter. So does development. Still, at some point, “raw” stops being an explanation and becomes the reason a team regrets its evaluation. A fresh start has to mean something Richardson may still have a path back, but it probably won’t come from simply changing jerseys. In February, it was reported that the Colts and Richardson had agreed to explore a trade, but no deal is guaranteed, and the market appears far less robust than his draft position might suggest. A new team would need a real plan: simplify his early reads, build confidence with quick throws, use designed runs selectively, and let his arm strength create explosive plays without asking him to play like a polished pocket passer overnight. He needs repetition, stability, and a coach willing to develop him rather than treat him as a ready-made starter. That cannot become an excuse to hide him from the hard parts of quarterbacking. Richardson still has to improve his footwork, accuracy, and processing. A new system can create better conditions. It cannot throw the ball for him. The clock is running out The Colts have moved forward with Daniel Jones, and Richardson’s future in Indianapolis is uncertain. He is still young enough for a team to take a low-cost chance, but the franchise-quarterback runway is shrinking. item.title: Garrett Wilson Yells At Geno Smith As Jets Lose Again
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The sideline scene on Sunday at MetLife Stadium was ugly, and it wasn’t just bad luck. Garrett Wilson, the Jets’ star receiver, lost his cool and yelled at quarterback Geno Smith during the fourth quarter. It happened right before the team lost to the Miami Dolphins, 28-25. The anger didn’t help a team that has now fallen to a 2-5 record for the season. According to the New York Post , Wilson unleashed his frustration for a few seconds while Smith just listened. Smith did not say a word back to his teammate before Wilson walked away. That silence speaks volumes about the state of the offense. The Jets were down 21-14 in the fourth quarter when they finally moved the ball. They drove 68 yards in 12 plays to get to the Miami one-yard line. But two bad runs and a sack of Smith stopped them cold. They settled for a field goal with 8:57 left and never got over the hump. A Quiet First Half Wilson’s anger is hard to ignore, but his lack of targets is the real story. Against Miami throughout the whole first half, he somehow escaped official targeting even a single time. He made one catch that got wiped out by a penalty. He didn’t record his first official catch until the third quarter. He finished the game with just two catches on three targets for 26 yards. Per the New York Post, this comes after a week where he caught only four passes for 44 yards in a loss in Foxborough. Facing a weak Miami offense, the defense surrendered 156 rushing yards, representing a massive problem. But the offense did not steal the game either. Wilson wanted to force his way into a larger part of the offense, but the anger did not work. The team fell to the Dolphins, who were previously winless. item.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo’s Brothers Proving a Painful Truth
item.description: Professional basketball players Giannis Antetokounmpo, Alex Antetokounmpo, Thanasis Antetokounmpo pose for a photo before ringing the closing bell at New York Stock Exchange on March 31, 2023 in New York City. Getty Giannis Antetokounmpo was the big move of the offseason for the Miami Heat, a blockbuster trade to acquire him from the Milwaukee Bucks. It was notable, in a small sense, who didn’t come along with Giannis — his brothers Thanasis and Alex, who have both worn a Bucks uniform, as well. His brother Kostas has played in the NBA, too. For years, Giannis and Thanasis were teammates in Milwaukee — Thanasis actually as the oldest of the brothers. Alex and Kostas both got much smaller NBA cameos but also got a chance at the highest level. But so far this season, Giannis is the only Antetokounmpo remaining in the NBA, and he’s also proving a painful truth. There was obviously curiosity through the years about whether Antetokounmpo’s brothers were around in Milwaukee more for the superstar than for their contributions. And while it totally makes sense that the Bucks wanted to keep Giannis happy, the performances of the brothers so far this season across the Atlantic certainly proves that true. Where Are Giannis’ Brothers? All three Antetokounmpo brothers that are playing professional basketball outside the NBA right now are playing in Greece. Thanasis is playing for Aris Midea Thessaloniki. He’s teammates there with Kostas. Alex is suiting up for ASP Promitheas Patras. Brother Stats It’s in the statistics that it’s quickly clear these brothers may not have quite been NBA-level players in the long run. Thanasis is so far averaging just 2.0 points, 1.0 rebounds, 0.6 assists and 1.0 steals per game in limited minutes. He’s 34 years old, so maybe he deserves a pass, particularly after injury trouble in the latter stages of his Bucks career — but still, you might expect more from him in the Greek league. Kostas has done a bit better as his teammate. He’s the biggest of the non-Giannis brothers and so can impact the game more in the frontcourt. So far this season, Kostas is putting up 3.6 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.1 blocks per game while shooting 61.9% from the floor. Alex, 25, has been quiet for his club in the early going, putting up 2.3 points and 1.0 rebounds per game. There’s nothing to really suggest that the Antetokoun-bros are going to all of a sudden catch fire, either. They’re all quality basketball players who were likely a bit out of their depth in the NBA. They’re not back in the country they grew up in getting to keep playing the game they love. There’s nothing wrong about any of the journey for the Antetokounmpo family, who defied the odds a lot of steps along the way. It’s just pretty clear at this point that Giannis may have helped his brothers get their NBA chances.
